----- FILE: web\src\components\DueCountdown.tsx -----
// NEW: "Due today / Due tomorrow / Due in N days / Overdue by N days".
// It re-renders ONCE just after each Johannesburg midnight, not every second (it only shows days).
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
import { dueCountdown, msUntilNextSaMidnight } from '@/lib/countdown'

export function DueCountdown({ due, cycleStatus }: { due: string; cycleStatus: string }) {
  const [now, setNow] = useState(() => new Date())

  useEffect(() => {
    if (cycleStatus !== 'Open') return // Closed / PaidOut cycles have no countdown, so no timer
    // setTimeout (not setInterval): one timer for the next SA midnight. +50ms lands just after it.
    const id = setTimeout(() => setNow(new Date()), msUntilNextSaMidnight(now) + 50)
    return () => clearTimeout(id) // cleanup: StrictMode and unmounting must not leave a timer behind
    // The effect READS `now`, so it must run again when `now` changes: that schedules the next midnight.
  }, [now, cycleStatus])

  const text = dueCountdown(due, now, cycleStatus)
  if (text === null) return null
  return <p className="text-sm font-medium">{text}</p>
}

----- FILE: web\src\components\ErrorView.tsx -----
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { describeError, rateLimitMessage } from '../lib/errorMessages';

// Counts down from "start" seconds; its timer is cleared when the component unmounts
function useCountdown(start: number | null): number | null {
  const [endsAt] = useState(() => (start === null ? null : Date.now() + start * 1000));
  const [now, setNow] = useState(() => Date.now());
  useEffect(() => {
    if (endsAt === null) return;
    const id = setInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, [endsAt]);
  return endsAt === null ? null : Math.max(0, Math.ceil((endsAt - now) / 1000));
}

// Reference the member can select and copy and read out to support
export function Reference({ id }: { id: string | null }) {
  if (!id) {
    return <p style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>No reference available (the request never reached RondiTrack).</p>;
  }
  return (
    <p style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>
      Reference: <code style={{ fontFamily: 'monospace', userSelect: 'all' }}>{id}</code>
    </p>
  );
}

type Props = { error: unknown; onRetry?: () => void; onBack?: () => void };

// The ONE error view every screen uses
export function ErrorView({ error, onRetry, onBack }: Props) {
  const d = describeError(error);
  const seconds = useCountdown(d.retryAfterSeconds);

  // Session ended: App shows the sign-in form, so we show nothing here (no stacked error)
  if (d.kind === 'sessionEnded') return null;

  const message =
    d.kind === 'rateLimited' && seconds !== null
      ? seconds > 0
        ? rateLimitMessage(seconds)
        : 'You can try again now.'
      : d.message;

  return (
    <div role="alert" style={{ border: '1px solid #c33', padding: 16, borderRadius: 8, margin: '16px 0' }}>
      <h2 style={{ marginTop: 0 }}>{d.title}</h2>
      <p>{message}</p>
      {d.kind === 'notFound' && onBack && <button onClick={onBack}>Back to my stokvels</button>}
      {d.kind !== 'notFound' && onRetry && (
        // for a 429 the button stays disabled until the countdown reaches zero
        <button onClick={onRetry} disabled={seconds !== null && seconds > 0}>
          Try again
        </button>
      )}
      <Reference id={d.correlationId} />
    </div>
  );
}

----- FILE: web\src\components\LoginForm.tsx -----
import { useState } from 'react';
import { login } from '../auth/session';
import { describeError } from '../lib/errorMessages';
import { Reference } from './ErrorView';

export function LoginForm({ onSignedIn }: { onSignedIn: () => void }) {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('');
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('');
  const [error, setError] = useState<unknown>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);

  async function submit(e: React.FormEvent) {
    e.preventDefault();
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await login(email, password);
      onSignedIn();
    } catch (err) {
      setError(err); // shown through describeError below
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  const d = error ? describeError(error, 'login') : null;

  return (
    <form onSubmit={submit} style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8, maxWidth: 320 }}>
      <h1>Sign in to RondiTrack</h1>
      <label htmlFor="email">Email</label>
      <input id="email" type="email" value={email} onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
      {d?.fieldErrors.email?.map((m) => <small key={m}>{m}</small>)}
      <label htmlFor="password">Password</label>
      <input id="password" type="password" value={password} onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)} />
      {d?.fieldErrors.password?.map((m) => <small key={m}>{m}</small>)}
      {d && d.kind !== 'validation' && (
        <div role="alert">
          <p>{d.message}</p>
          <Reference id={d.correlationId} />
        </div>
      )}
      <button type="submit" disabled={busy}>{busy ? 'Signing inâ€¦' : 'Sign in'}</button>
    </form>
  );
}

----- FILE: web\src\components\StatusBadge.tsx -----
// NEW: one badge for every RondiTrack status. It takes a KIND as well as a status, because
// "Paid" (a member's claim) and "PaidOut" (the whole pot went out) must never look alike.
// Every badge shows a WORD + an ICON + a tone: never colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
import {
  Banknote, Check, CheckCheck, CircleDot, Clock, Info, Lock, TriangleAlert, type LucideIcon,
} from 'lucide-react'
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { formatCents } from '@/lib/money'

export type StatusKind = 'cycle' | 'contribution'

// Light + dark colour pairs chosen for 4.5:1 text contrast. Measure them in DevTools (README table).
const TONE = {
  indigo: 'border-indigo-300 bg-indigo-100 text-indigo-900 dark:border-indigo-800 dark:bg-indigo-950 dark:text-indigo-200',
  slate: 'border-slate-300 bg-slate-100 text-slate-900 dark:border-slate-600 dark:bg-slate-800 dark:text-slate-100',
  violet: 'border-violet-300 bg-violet-100 text-violet-900 dark:border-violet-800 dark:bg-violet-950 dark:text-violet-200',
  amber: 'border-amber-300 bg-amber-100 text-amber-900 dark:border-amber-800 dark:bg-amber-950 dark:text-amber-200',
  sky: 'border-sky-300 bg-sky-100 text-sky-900 dark:border-sky-800 dark:bg-sky-950 dark:text-sky-200',
  green: 'border-green-300 bg-green-100 text-green-900 dark:border-green-800 dark:bg-green-950 dark:text-green-200',
  red: 'border-red-300 bg-red-100 text-red-900 dark:border-red-800 dark:bg-red-950 dark:text-red-200',
  neutral: 'border-border bg-muted text-foreground', // theme tokens for the "unknown" look
}

type Look = { label: string; Icon: LucideIcon; tone: string }

const CYCLE_LOOK = new Map<string, Look>([
  ['Open', { label: 'Open', Icon: CircleDot, tone: TONE.indigo }],
  ['Closed', { label: 'Closed', Icon: Lock, tone: TONE.slate }],
  ['PaidOut', { label: 'Paid out', Icon: Banknote, tone: TONE.violet }], // human words, not "PaidOut"
])

const CONTRIBUTION_LOOK = new Map<string, Look>([
  ['Pending', { label: 'Pending', Icon: Clock, tone: TONE.amber }],
  ['Paid', { label: 'Paid, awaiting check', Icon: Check, tone: TONE.sky }], // the member's claim
  ['Confirmed', { label: 'Confirmed', Icon: CheckCheck, tone: TONE.green }], // the treasurer's check
])

export function StatusBadge({ kind, status }: { kind: StatusKind; status: string }) {
  const table = kind === 'cycle' ? CYCLE_LOOK : CONTRIBUTION_LOOK
  // An unknown status shows its raw value in a neutral badge: no crash, no guess
  const look = table.get(status) ?? { label: status, Icon: Info, tone: TONE.neutral }
  const { label, Icon, tone } = look
  return (
    <Badge variant="outline" className={cn('h-auto gap-1 whitespace-normal text-left', tone)}>
      <Icon aria-hidden="true" className="size-3.5 shrink-0" />
      {label}
    </Badge>
  )
}

// Arrears badge: shows only when the caller really owes arrears. No arrears means no badge at all.
export function ArrearsBadge({ cents }: { cents: number | null | undefined }) {
  if (cents === null || cents === undefined || cents <= 0) return null
  return (
    <Badge variant="outline" className={cn('h-auto gap-1 whitespace-normal text-left', TONE.red)}>
      <TriangleAlert aria-hidden="true" className="size-3.5 shrink-0" />
      <span>
        In arrears: <span className="whitespace-nowrap">{formatCents(cents)}</span>
      </span>
    </Badge>
  )
}

----- FILE: web\src\components\StokvelScreen.tsx -----
import { useContributions, useCycles, useStokvel } from '../api/queries';
import { ContributionSection } from '../contributions/ContributionSection'; // NEW 7.4
import { formatCentsAsRand } from '../lib/rand';
import { ErrorView } from './ErrorView';
import { Skeleton } from './Skeleton';

// NOTE: do not give this component key={stokvelId}. Remounting would hide the keepPreviousData
// bug instead of fixing it, and the Part 4 proof test would no longer prove anything.
export function StokvelScreen({ stokvelId, onBack }: { stokvelId: string; onBack: () => void }) {
  const stokvel = useStokvel(stokvelId);
  const cycles = useCycles(stokvelId);

  // Show the open cycle, otherwise the newest one
  const sorted = cycles.data ? [...cycles.data].sort((a, b) => b.number - a.number) : [];
  const cycle = sorted.find((c) => c.status === 'Open') ?? sorted[0];

  const contributions = useContributions(stokvelId, cycle?.id);

  // 1) error state is checked FIRST so a 404 never leaves a spinner forever
  if (stokvel.isError || cycles.isError || contributions.isError) {
    const error = stokvel.error ?? cycles.error ?? contributions.error;
    return (
      <ErrorView
        error={error}
        onBack={onBack}
        onRetry={() => {
          void stokvel.refetch();
          void cycles.refetch();
          void contributions.refetch();
        }}
      />
    );
  }

  // 2) loading state: skeleton, never the old stokvel's rows
  if (stokvel.isPending || cycles.isPending) return <Skeleton label="Loading stokvel" />;

  // 3) empty state: no cycle yet
  if (!cycle) {
    return (
      <section>
        <h2>{stokvel.data.name}</h2>
        <p>
          No contribution cycle has been started yet. This is normal for a new stokvel. The
          treasurer can start the first cycle.
        </p>
      </section>
    );
  }

  if (contributions.isPending) return <Skeleton label="Loading contributions" />;

  const rows = contributions.data.pages.flatMap((page) => page.items);
  const totalCents = rows.reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.amountCents, 0);

  return (
    <section>
      <h2>{stokvel.data.name}</h2>
      <p>Cycle {cycle.number}</p>

      {/* NEW 7.4: the form (open cycle) or the reason there is no form (closed / paid out) */}
      <ContributionSection stokvelId={stokvelId} cycle={cycle} />

      {/* 3) empty state: cycle exists but nobody has paid yet */}
      {rows.length === 0 ? (
        <p>
          No contributions yet. This is normal for a new cycle. The treasurer can record the
          first contribution once a member pays in.
        </p>
      ) : (
        // 4) data state
        <>
          <p>Total shown: <strong>{formatCentsAsRand(totalCents)}</strong></p>
          <ul>
            {rows.map((c) => (
              <li key={c.id}>
                {c.memberName}: {formatCentsAsRand(c.amountCents)} ({c.status})
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
          {contributions.hasNextPage && (
            <button
              onClick={() => void contributions.fetchNextPage()}
              disabled={contributions.isFetchingNextPage}
            >
              {contributions.isFetchingNextPage ? 'Loading...' : 'Load more'}
            </button>
          )}
        </>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}

import { describe, it, expect, afterEach, beforeEach, vi } from 'vitest';
import { cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import { QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { createQueryClient } from '../lib/queryClient';
import { Dashboard } from './Dashboard';
import { formatCentsAsRand } from '../lib/rand';
import { __resetSessionForTests } from '../auth/session';
import { clearSelectedStokvel } from '../state/selectedStokvel';

const json = (data: unknown) =>
  new Response(JSON.stringify(data), { status: 200, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } });
const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

beforeEach(() => {
  __resetSessionForTests();
  clearSelectedStokvel();
  // Fake API matching my real routes. Stokvel "b" answers SLOWLY (150 ms) on every call.
  // If it answered instantly the bug could not appear and the test would prove nothing.
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', async (input: RequestInfo | URL) => {
    const path = new URL(input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)).pathname;
    if (path.endsWith('/auth/refresh')) return json({ accessToken: 'tok' });
    if (path.endsWith('/me/home')) return json({ stokvels: [{ stokvelId: 'a', name: 'Mabena Family' }, { stokvelId: 'b', name: 'Soweto Teachers' }] });
    if (path.endsWith('/api/v1/stokvels')) {
      return json([{ id: 'a', name: 'Mabena Family' }, { id: 'b', name: 'Soweto Teachers' }]);
    }
    const match = path.match(/\/api\/v1\/stokvels\/([^/]+)(?:\/cycles(?:\/([^/]+)\/contributions)?)?$/);
    if (!match) return new Response(null, { status: 404 });
    const [, id, cycleId] = match;
    if (id === 'b') await sleep(150);

    if (cycleId) {
      return json({
        items: [id === 'a'
          ? { id: 'a1', memberName: 'Thandi Mabena', amountCents: 11111, status: 'Paid' }
          : { id: 'b1', memberName: 'Sipho Dlamini', amountCents: 22222, status: 'Paid' }],
        nextPageToken: '',
      });
    }
    if (path.endsWith('/cycles')) {
      return json([{ id: `${id}-c1`, number: 1, status: 'Open' }]);
    }
    return json({ id, name: id === 'a' ? 'Mabena Family' : 'Soweto Teachers' });
  });
});

afterEach(() => {
  cleanup();
  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
});

describe('stokvel switching', () => {
  it('never shows the previous stokvel amounts right after switching', async () => {
    render(
      <QueryClientProvider client={createQueryClient()}>
        <Dashboard />
      </QueryClientProvider>,
    );

    // stokvel A is on screen
    await screen.findByText(/Thandi Mabena/);
    expect(document.body.textContent).toContain(formatCentsAsRand(11111));

    // switch to B, then look IMMEDIATELY (B is still loading)
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText('Stokvel'), { target: { value: 'b' } });
    expect(document.body.textContent).not.toContain(formatCentsAsRand(11111));
    expect(document.body.textContent).not.toContain('Thandi Mabena');

    // later, B's own data arrives
    // Wait until B's heading shows; at that moment A's rows must NOT be under it
    await screen.findByRole('heading', { name: 'Soweto Teachers' });
    expect(document.body.textContent).not.toContain(formatCentsAsRand(11111));
    await screen.findByText(/Sipho Dlamini/);
    expect(document.body.textContent).toContain(formatCentsAsRand(22222));
  });
});

// NEW: Light / Dark / System buttons. aria-pressed tells a screen reader which one is on.
import { Monitor, Moon, Sun } from 'lucide-react'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { useTheme, type Theme } from '@/theme/theme-context'

const OPTIONS: { value: Theme; label: string; Icon: typeof Sun }[] = [
  { value: 'light', label: 'Light', Icon: Sun },
  { value: 'dark', label: 'Dark', Icon: Moon },
  { value: 'system', label: 'System', Icon: Monitor },
]

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme()
  return (
    <div role="group" aria-label="Colour theme" className="flex flex-wrap gap-1">
      {OPTIONS.map(({ value, label, Icon }) => (
        <Button
          key={value}
          type="button"
          size="sm"
          variant={theme === value ? 'default' : 'outline'}
          aria-pressed={theme === value}
          onClick={() => setTheme(value)}
        >
          <Icon aria-hidden="true" />
          {label}
        </Button>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

function CardHeader({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<"div">) {
  return (
    <div

// NEW 7.4: the form. React Hook Form + Zod + useMutation (mutateAsync awaited in the submit handler).
import { useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form';
import { zodResolver } from '@hookform/resolvers/zod';
import { z } from 'zod';
import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { ApiError } from '../api/apiError';
import { queryKeys } from '../api/queryKeys';
import { Reference } from '../components/ErrorView';
import { describeError, parseRetryAfter, rateLimitMessage } from '../lib/errorMessages';
import { formatCents } from '../lib/money';
import { centsToInput, parseRandsToCents } from '../lib/rands';
import { createContributionSubmitter } from './submitContribution';

export type Member = { id: string; name: string };

type Props = {
  stokvelId: string;
  cycleId: string;
  cycleNumber: number;
  isTreasurer: boolean; // role for THIS stokvel, from /me/home
  meId: string;
  members: Member[]; // only used by a Treasurer
  owedCents: number; // what the member still owes, used to prefill
};

// Zod checks the typed text with OUR parser, so "150.505" is refused instead of rounded
const schema = z.object({
  memberId: z.string().min(1, 'Choose a member'),
  amount: z
    .string()
    .refine((v) => parseRandsToCents(v) !== null, 'Enter a valid amount, like 150.50 (at most 2 decimals)')
    .refine((v) => (parseRandsToCents(v) ?? 0) > 0, 'The amount must be more than R0'),
});
type FormValues = z.infer<typeof schema>;

// Keys in a 400 "errors" map (lower-case, as describeError gives them) -> our field names.
// Any key we do not know is shown at the top of the form.
const FIELD_MAP: Record<string, keyof FormValues> = {
  amountincents: 'amount',
  userid: 'memberId',
};

type Shown = {
  lines: string[];
  correlationId: string | null;
  fieldErrors: Record<string, string[]>;
  mayHaveLanded: boolean;
};

// Turns any error into what the person sees. Reuses describeError for everything it already knows.
function explain(error: unknown): Shown {
  const d = describeError(error);
  const detail =
    error instanceof ApiError && typeof error.problem?.detail === 'string' ? error.problem.detail : null;
  const base = { correlationId: d.correlationId, fieldErrors: d.fieldErrors };

  // No answer at all: the payment may or may not have been recorded
  if (d.kind === 'network') {
    return {
      ...base,
      mayHaveLanded: true,
      lines: [
        'We did not get an answer, so your payment may have gone through. Your details are kept. Trying again is safe: it will not pay twice.',
      ],
    };
  }
  if (error instanceof ApiError && error.status === 429) {
    return {
      ...base,
      mayHaveLanded: true,
      lines: [`${rateLimitMessage(parseRetryAfter(error.retryAfter))} Your details are kept, and trying again is safe.`],
    };
  }
  if (error instanceof ApiError && error.status >= 500) {
    return {
      ...base,
      mayHaveLanded: true,
      lines: [
        'RondiTrack had a problem, so your payment may have gone through. Your details are kept. Trying again is safe: it will not pay twice.',
      ],
    };
  }
  // 400 / 403 / 409 / 422: show the API's own detail (it explains why)
  if (error instanceof ApiError && [400, 403, 409, 422].includes(error.status)) {
    return { ...base, mayHaveLanded: false, lines: [detail ?? d.message] };
  }
  return { ...base, mayHaveLanded: false, lines: [d.message] };
}

export function ContributionForm({ stokvelId, cycleId, cycleNumber, isTreasurer, meId, members, owedCents }: Props) {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();

  // One submitter (and so one key keeper) per form. This initialiser makes NO key, so StrictMode is safe.
  const [submitter] = useState(() => createContributionSubmitter());
  const inFlight = useRef(false); // stops a double-click from sending two requests
  const [shown, setShown] = useState<Shown | null>(null);
  const [confirmation, setConfirmation] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const {
    register,
    handleSubmit,
    reset,
    setError,
    clearErrors,
    formState: { errors, isSubmitting },
  } = useForm<FormValues>({
    resolver: zodResolver(schema),
    // Prefill with what the member still owes (nothing when they owe nothing)
    defaultValues: { memberId: meId, amount: owedCents > 0 ? centsToInput(owedCents) : '' },
  });

  const mutation = useMutation({ mutationFn: submitter });

  const onSubmit = async (values: FormValues) => {
    if (inFlight.current) return; // a second click in the same moment does nothing
    inFlight.current = true;
    setShown(null);
    setConfirmation(null);
    clearErrors();

    try {
      const amountInCents = parseRandsToCents(values.amount);
      if (amountInCents === null) return; // Zod already refused this, so it cannot happen

      await mutation.mutateAsync({ stokvelId, cycleId, userId: values.memberId, amountInCents });

      // Wait for the refetch, so the button stays disabled until the new numbers are on screen
      await Promise.all([
        queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.home }),
        queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.contributions(stokvelId, cycleId) }),
      ]);

      const who =
        values.memberId === meId && !isTreasurer
          ? 'you'
          : (members.find((m) => m.id === values.memberId)?.name ?? 'the member');
      setConfirmation(`Recorded ${formatCents(amountInCents)} for ${who} in Cycle ${cycleNumber}.`);
      // keepFieldsRef: the React Compiler and reset() do not agree without it
      reset({ memberId: meId, amount: '' }, { keepFieldsRef: true });
    } catch (error) {
      const result = explain(error);
      setShown(result);
      const extra: string[] = [];
      for (const [key, messages] of Object.entries(result.fieldErrors)) {
        const field = FIELD_MAP[key];
        if (field) setError(field, { message: messages.join(' ') }); // goes under its field
        else extra.push(`${key}: ${messages.join(' ')}`); // unknown key goes to the top
      }
      if (extra.length > 0) setShown({ ...result, lines: [...result.lines, ...extra] });
    } finally {
      inFlight.current = false;
    }
  };

  return (
    <form onSubmit={(event) => void handleSubmit(onSubmit)(event)} noValidate style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8, margin: '16px 0' }}>
      <h3>Record a contribution</h3>

      {shown && (
        <div role="alert" style={{ border: '1px solid #c33', padding: 12, borderRadius: 8 }}>
          {shown.lines.map((line) => (
            <p key={line}>{line}</p>
          ))}
          <Reference id={shown.correlationId} />
        </div>
      )}
      {confirmation && <p role="status">{confirmation}</p>}

      {/* A Member never sees the picker. Hiding it is only convenience: the API's 403 still protects the rule. */}
      {isTreasurer && (
        <div>
          <label htmlFor="memberId">Member</label>{' '}
          <select id="memberId" {...register('memberId')}>
            {members.map((m) => (
              <option key={m.id} value={m.id}>
                {m.name}
              </option>
            ))}
          </select>
          {errors.memberId && <p role="alert">{errors.memberId.message}</p>}
        </div>
      )}

      <div>
        <label htmlFor="amount">Amount (rands)</label>{' '}
        <input id="amount" inputMode="decimal" autoComplete="off" {...register('amount')} />
        {errors.amount && <p role="alert">{errors.amount.message}</p>}
      </div>

      {/* Disabled from the click until the API answered AND the queries refetched */}
      <button type="submit" disabled={isSubmitting}>
        {isSubmitting ? 'Recording...' : shown?.mayHaveLanded ? 'Try again' : 'Record contribution'}
      </button>
    </form>
  );
}

----- FILE: web\src\contributions\ContributionSection.tsx -----
// NEW 7.4: shows the form only on an OPEN cycle (otherwise a sentence saying why) and works out who is who.
import { useHome, useMembers } from '../api/queries';
import { currentUserId } from '../auth/session';
import { ErrorView } from '../components/ErrorView';
import { Skeleton } from '../components/Skeleton';
import { isTreasurer } from '../lib/roles';
import { ContributionForm, type Member } from './ContributionForm';

type Props = {
  stokvelId: string;
  cycle: { id: string; number: number; status: string };
};

// Reads a member's name without hand-writing the API type (the API calls it fullName)
function toMember(u: unknown): Member | null {
  const o = u as Record<string, unknown>;
  const id = typeof o.id === 'string' ? o.id : typeof o.userId === 'string' ? o.userId : null;
  const name = [o.fullName, o.name, o.email].find((v): v is string => typeof v === 'string');
  return id ? { id, name: name ?? id } : null;
}

export function ContributionSection({ stokvelId, cycle }: Props) {
  const home = useHome();
  const mine = home.data?.stokvels.find((s) => s.stokvelId === stokvelId);
  const treasurer = mine ? isTreasurer(mine.role) : false;
  const membersQuery = useMembers(stokvelId, treasurer);

  // Closed or PaidOut: no form, just the reason
  if (cycle.status !== 'Open') {
    return (
      <p>
        Cycle {cycle.number} is {cycle.status === 'PaidOut' ? 'paid out' : 'closed'}, so contributions can no longer be
        recorded.
      </p>
    );
  }

  if (home.isPending) return <Skeleton label="Loading contribution form" />;
  if (home.isError) return <ErrorView error={home.error} onRetry={() => void home.refetch()} />;
  if (!mine) return <p>You are not a member of this stokvel, so you cannot record a contribution here.</p>;

  const meId = currentUserId();
  if (!meId) return <p>Please sign in again to record a contribution.</p>;

  if (treasurer && membersQuery.isPending) return <Skeleton label="Loading members" />;
  if (treasurer && membersQuery.isError) {
    return <ErrorView error={membersQuery.error} onRetry={() => void membersQuery.refetch()} />;
  }

  const members = (membersQuery.data?.pages.flatMap((p) => p.items) ?? [])
    .map(toMember)
    .filter((m): m is Member => m !== null);

  return (
    <ContributionForm
      stokvelId={stokvelId}
      cycleId={cycle.id}
      cycleNumber={cycle.number}
      isTreasurer={treasurer}
      meId={meId}
      members={members}
      owedCents={mine.owedCents}
    />
  );
}

----- FILE: web\src\contributions\intentKey.ts -----
// NEW 7.4: remembers the Idempotency-Key for ONE intent to pay.
// Plain TypeScript (no React) so the MSW tests drive the real thing.
export function createIntentKeeper(makeKey: () => string = () => crypto.randomUUID()) {
  // The key lives inside this keeper (one per form), not in a module variable and not in the TanStack cache.
  let current: { key: string; fingerprint: string } | null = null;

  return {
    // Same fingerprint (same member + cycle + amount) = same key. Anything changed = a NEW key.
    // The key is only made when someone submits, never during render, so StrictMode's double render can't make two.
    keyFor(fingerprint: string): string {
      if (!current || current.fingerprint !== fingerprint) {
        current = { key: makeKey(), fingerprint };
      }
      return current.key;
    },
    // Forget the key: the intent finished (success) or was definitely rejected (400/403/404/409/422).
    release() {
      current = null;
    },
  };
}

// @vitest-environment node
// NEW 7.4: the real generated client + authFetch + key logic run. ONLY the network is fake (MSW).
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node';
import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { ApiError } from '../api/apiError';
import { API_BASE_URL } from '../api/config';
import { __resetSessionForTests, login } from '../auth/session';
import { parseRetryAfter } from '../lib/errorMessages';
import { parseRandsToCents } from '../lib/rands';
import { createIntentKeeper } from './intentKey';
import { createContributionSubmitter } from './submitContribution';

const CONTRIBUTIONS = `${API_BASE_URL}/api/v1/stokvels/:stokvelId/cycles/:cycleId/contributions`;
const recorded = { id: 'c1', stokvelId: 's1', userId: 'm1', cycleId: 'cy1', amount: 150.5, recordedAtUtc: '2026-10-25T10:00:00Z' };

// What the fake server saw on each request to the contributions endpoint
let keysSeen: (string | null)[] = [];
let authSeen: (string | null)[] = [];
let bodiesSeen: unknown[] = [];
let attempt = 0;

const server = setupServer(
  // the real login() runs against this
  http.post(`${API_BASE_URL}/api/v1/auth/login`, () => HttpResponse.json({ accessToken: 'token-1' })),
  // authFetch's refresh runs against this
  http.post(`${API_BASE_URL}/api/v1/auth/refresh`, () => HttpResponse.json({ accessToken: 'token-2' })),
);

beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' })); // a request nobody expected fails the test
afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers());
afterAll(() => server.close());

beforeEach(async () => {
  keysSeen = [];
  authSeen = [];
  bodiesSeen = [];
  attempt = 0;
  __resetSessionForTests();
  await login('treasurer@test.local', 'password'); // real login, fake network
});

// Records what arrived, then lets each test choose the response for attempt n
function contributionsHandler(respond: (n: number) => Response) {
  return http.post(CONTRIBUTIONS, async ({ request }) => {
    keysSeen.push(request.headers.get('Idempotency-Key'));
    authSeen.push(request.headers.get('Authorization'));
    bodiesSeen.push(await request.clone().json());
    attempt++;
    return respond(attempt);
  });
}

const created = () => HttpResponse.json(recorded, { status: 201 });
const input = { stokvelId: 's1', cycleId: 'cy1', userId: 'm1', amountInCents: 15050 };

describe('recording a contribution', () => {
  it('1. a retry after a network error sends the same key', async () => {
    // First attempt never gets an answer: a dropped connection
    server.use(contributionsHandler((n) => (n === 1 ? HttpResponse.error() : created())));
    const submit = createContributionSubmitter();

    await expect(submit(input)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(TypeError);
    await submit(input); // the person clicks "Try again", nothing changed

    expect(keysSeen).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(keysSeen[0]).not.toBeNull();
    expect(keysSeen[1]).not.toBeNull();
    expect(keysSeen[0]).toBe(keysSeen[1]);
  });

  it('2. the next contribution gets a new key', async () => {
    server.use(contributionsHandler(() => created()));
    const submit = createContributionSubmitter();

    await submit(input);
    await submit(input); // a second, new payment

    expect(keysSeen).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(keysSeen[0]).not.toBe(keysSeen[1]);
  });

  it('3. a 429 keeps the key and exposes the wait', async () => {
    server.use(
      contributionsHandler((n) =>
        n === 1
          ? HttpResponse.json({ title: 'Too many requests' }, { status: 429, headers: { 'Retry-After': '1' } })
          : created(),
      ),
    );
    const submit = createContributionSubmitter();

    const error = await submit(input).catch((e: unknown) => e);
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(ApiError);
    expect((error as ApiError).status).toBe(429);
    expect(parseRetryAfter((error as ApiError).retryAfter)).toBe(1); // the form shows this wait

    await submit(input); // after the wait
    expect(keysSeen[0]).not.toBeNull();
    expect(keysSeen[0]).toBe(keysSeen[1]);
  });

  it('4. changing the amount after a failure is a new intent', async () => {
    server.use(contributionsHandler((n) => (n === 1 ? HttpResponse.error() : created())));
    const submit = createContributionSubmitter();

    await expect(submit(input)).rejects.toBeDefined();
    await submit({ ...input, amountInCents: 20000 }); // the person corrected the amount

    expect(keysSeen[0]).not.toBe(keysSeen[1]);
    expect(bodiesSeen[1]).toMatchObject({ amountInCents: 20000 });
  });

  it('5. a 401 retry keeps the key and uses the new token', async () => {
    server.use(
      contributionsHandler((n) => (n === 1 ? new HttpResponse(null, { status: 401 }) : created())),
    );
    const submit = createContributionSubmitter();

    await submit(input); // authFetch refreshes and retries by itself

    expect(keysSeen).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(keysSeen[0]).not.toBeNull();
    expect(keysSeen[1]).toBe(keysSeen[0]);
    expect(authSeen[0]).toBe('Bearer token-1');
    expect(authSeen[1]).toBe('Bearer token-2'); // the new token
  });

  it('6. cents survive the trip: "150.50" is sent as the number 15050', async () => {
    server.use(contributionsHandler(() => created()));
    const submit = createContributionSubmitter();

    await submit({ ...input, amountInCents: parseRandsToCents('150.50')! });

    const body = bodiesSeen[0] as { amountInCents: unknown };
    expect(body.amountInCents).toBe(15050);
    expect(typeof body.amountInCents).toBe('number');
  });
});

describe('StrictMode safety', () => {
  it('no key is made until someone submits, so a double render cannot make two', () => {
    const makeKey = vi.fn(() => 'k1');
    const keeper = createIntentKeeper(makeKey);
    expect(makeKey).not.toHaveBeenCalled(); // creating the keeper (what StrictMode runs twice) makes no key
    keeper.keyFor('a');
    keeper.keyFor('a');
    expect(makeKey).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1); // one intent, one key
  });
});

----- FILE: web\src\contributions\submitContribution.ts -----
// NEW 7.4: ties the key logic to the generated client. One submitter per form instance.
import { ApiError } from '../api/apiError';
import { api, unwrap } from '../api/client';
import { createIntentKeeper } from './intentKey';

export type SubmitInput = {
  stokvelId: string;
  cycleId: string;
  userId: string; // the member the money is for (the API calls it userId)
  amountInCents: number; // integer cents, always a number
};

// Did we get NO real answer, so the money may have been recorded? Then the key must be kept for the retry.
// 401 (authFetch already tried a refresh), 429 (a rejected request does not use up its key), 5xx, dropped connection.
// A real answer (400, 403, 404, 409, 422) means we know nothing was recorded, so the next try is a fresh intent.
export function keepsKey(error: unknown): boolean {
  if (error instanceof ApiError) {
    return error.status === 401 || error.status === 429 || error.status >= 500;
  }
  return error instanceof TypeError; // fetch rejected: network error, outcome unknown
}

export function createContributionSubmitter() {
  const keeper = createIntentKeeper();

  return async function submit(input: SubmitInput) {
    // Same member + cycle + amount = same intent = same key. Change any of them = new key.
    const fingerprint = `${input.stokvelId}|${input.cycleId}|${input.userId}|${input.amountInCents}`;
    const idempotencyKey = keeper.keyFor(fingerprint);

    try {
      // The header comes from the OpenAPI document, so the generated client types and sends it.
      const result = await unwrap(
        await api.POST('/api/v1/stokvels/{stokvelId}/cycles/{cycleId}/contributions', {
          params: {
            path: { stokvelId: input.stokvelId, cycleId: input.cycleId },
            header: { 'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey },
          },
          body: { userId: input.userId, amountInCents: input.amountInCents },
        }),
      );
      keeper.release(); // success (even a replayed 201): this intent is done, the next payment gets a NEW key
      return result;
    } catch (error) {
      if (!keepsKey(error)) keeper.release();
      throw error;
    }
  };
}

----- FILE: web\src\lib\countdown.test.ts -----
// NEW: boundary tests for the due-date maths. Every test passes its own "now".
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { dueCountdown, dueDateToDeadline, msUntilNextSaMidnight } from './countdown'

const at = (iso: string) => new Date(iso)

describe('dueDateToDeadline', () => {
  it('turns a calendar date into the END of that day in Johannesburg', () => {
    expect(dueDateToDeadline('2026-10-31').toISOString()).toBe('2026-10-31T22:00:00.000Z')
  })

  it('does not treat the date as UTC midnight', () => {
    expect(dueDateToDeadline('2026-10-31').toISOString()).not.toBe('2026-10-31T00:00:00.000Z')
  })

  it('uses the South African day of an instant', () => {
    expect(dueDateToDeadline('2026-10-31T21:59:59Z').toISOString()).toBe('2026-10-31T22:00:00.000Z')
  })

  it('throws on a value that is not a date', () => {
    expect(() => dueDateToDeadline('banana')).toThrow()
  })
})

describe('dueCountdown', () => {
  it('23:30 SAST on the due date is Due today, not overdue', () => {
    expect(dueCountdown('2026-10-31', at('2026-10-31T21:30:00Z'), 'Open')).toBe('Due today')
  })

  it('00:30 SAST on the due date is Due today', () => {
    expect(dueCountdown('2026-10-31', at('2026-10-30T22:30:00Z'), 'Open')).toBe('Due today')
  })

  it('one second after the deadline is Overdue by 1 day', () => {
    expect(dueCountdown('2026-10-31', at('2026-10-31T22:00:01Z'), 'Open')).toBe('Overdue by 1 day')
  })

  it('counts several days overdue', () => {
    expect(dueCountdown('2026-10-31', at('2026-11-03T10:00:00Z'), 'Open')).toBe('Overdue by 3 days')
  })

  it('the day before is Due tomorrow', () => {
    expect(dueCountdown('2026-10-31', at('2026-10-30T10:00:00Z'), 'Open')).toBe('Due tomorrow')
  })

  it('later shows Due in N days', () => {
    expect(dueCountdown('2026-10-31', at('2026-10-26T10:00:00Z'), 'Open')).toBe('Due in 5 days')
  })

  it('shows no countdown for Closed or PaidOut cycles', () => {
    expect(dueCountdown('2026-10-31', at('2026-10-31T10:00:00Z'), 'Closed')).toBeNull()
    expect(dueCountdown('2026-10-31', at('2026-10-31T10:00:00Z'), 'PaidOut')).toBeNull()
  })
})

describe('msUntilNextSaMidnight', () => {
  it('from 23:30 SAST it is 30 minutes', () => {
    expect(msUntilNextSaMidnight(at('2026-10-31T21:30:00Z'))).toBe(30 * 60 * 1000)
  })

  it('from exactly midnight it is 24 hours, not 0', () => {
    expect(msUntilNextSaMidnight(at('2026-10-31T22:00:00Z'))).toBe(24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)
  })
})

----- FILE: web\src\lib\countdown.ts -----
// NEW: South African due-date maths. Pure functions: "now" is always passed in, never read here.
const MS_PER_DAY = 86_400_000
// South Africa is UTC+2 all year with no daylight saving since 1944, so a fixed offset is safe.
const SA_OFFSET_MS = 2 * 3_600_000
const CALENDAR_DATE = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/

// Which South African calendar day an instant falls on (a whole number of days since 1970).
export function saDayIndex(instant: Date): number {
  return Math.floor((instant.getTime() + SA_OFFSET_MS) / MS_PER_DAY)
}

// The South African calendar day a due date means. "2026-10-31" is that day itself;
// an instant like "2026-10-31T21:59:59Z" is the SA day it falls on.
function dueDayIndex(due: string): number {
  if (CALENDAR_DATE.test(due)) {
    const year = Number(due.slice(0, 4))
    const month = Number(due.slice(5, 7))
    const day = Number(due.slice(8, 10))
    return Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day) / MS_PER_DAY
  }
  const instant = new Date(due)
  if (Number.isNaN(instant.getTime())) throw new Error(`not a valid due date: ${due}`)
  return saDayIndex(instant)
}

// The moment the due day ENDS in Johannesburg. "2026-10-31" -> 2026-10-31T22:00:00Z (not 00:00Z).
export function dueDateToDeadline(due: string): Date {
  return new Date((dueDayIndex(due) + 1) * MS_PER_DAY - SA_OFFSET_MS)
}

// Milliseconds until the next Johannesburg midnight. Exactly at midnight it returns 24 hours, never 0.
export function msUntilNextSaMidnight(now: Date): number {
  return (saDayIndex(now) + 1) * MS_PER_DAY - SA_OFFSET_MS - now.getTime()
}

function days(n: number): string {
  return n === 1 ? 'day' : 'days'
}

// The countdown words, or null when no countdown should show (cycle Closed or PaidOut).
export function dueCountdown(due: string, now: Date, cycleStatus: string): string | null {
  if (cycleStatus !== 'Open') return null

  if (now.getTime() >= dueDateToDeadline(due).getTime()) {
    const late = saDayIndex(now) - dueDayIndex(due)
    return `Overdue by ${late} ${days(late)}`
  }

  const left = dueDayIndex(due) - saDayIndex(now)
  if (left === 0) return 'Due today'
  if (left === 1) return 'Due tomorrow'
  return `Due in ${left} days`
}

----- FILE: web\src\lib\dates.ts -----
// NEW: formats dates in South African time, whatever time zone the laptop is set to.
const TIME_ZONE = 'Africa/Johannesburg'

// "01 Nov 2026, 00:30"
const dateTimeFormatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-ZA', {
  dateStyle: 'medium',
  timeStyle: 'short',
  timeZone: TIME_ZONE,
})

// "01 Nov 2026"
const dateFormatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-ZA', {
  dateStyle: 'medium',
  timeZone: TIME_ZONE,
})

// Matches a plain calendar date like "2026-10-31" (no time, no Z)
const CALENDAR_DATE = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/

function toDate(value: string): Date {
  // A plain calendar date is already a South African day. Noon UTC (14:00 in SA)
  // means no time zone can push it onto the wrong day.
  const date = CALENDAR_DATE.test(value) ? new Date(`${value}T12:00:00Z`) : new Date(value)
  if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) {
    throw new Error(`not a valid date: ${value}`)
  }
  return date
}

// For UTC instants like "2026-10-31T22:30:00Z" (date AND time, in SA time)
export function formatDateTime(value: string): string {
  return dateTimeFormatter.format(toDate(value))
}

// Date only. Works with both a UTC instant and a calendar date
export function formatDate(value: string): string {
  return dateFormatter.format(toDate(value))
}

----- FILE: web\src\lib\errorMessages.ts -----
import { ApiError } from '../api/apiError';

export type ErrorKind =
  | 'network'
  | 'rateLimited'
  | 'badCredentials'
  | 'sessionEnded'
  | 'notFound'
  | 'validation'
  | 'generic';

export type DescribedError = {
  kind: ErrorKind;
  title: string;
  message: string;
  correlationId: string | null; // null = there is no reference to show
  retryAfterSeconds: number | null;
  fieldErrors: Record<string, string[]>; // keys are lower-case, e.g. "email"
};

// Retry-After is either seconds ("23") or an HTTP date. Returns seconds or null.
export function parseRetryAfter(header: string | null | undefined, now: number = Date.now()): number | null {
  if (!header) return null;
  const text = header.trim();
  if (/^\d+$/.test(text)) return Number(text);
  const when = Date.parse(text);
  if (Number.isNaN(when)) return null;
  return Math.max(0, Math.ceil((when - now) / 1000)); // date in the past = 0
}

export function rateLimitMessage(seconds: number | null): string {
  if (seconds === null) return 'Too many requests. Please wait a moment and try again.';
  return `Too many requests. Try again in ${seconds} ${seconds === 1 ? 'second' : 'seconds'}.`;
}

const asString = (v: unknown): string | null => (typeof v === 'string' && v ? v : null);

// Turns ANY error into plain words. Never uses the "detail" field (it can leak internals on a 500).
export function describeError(error: unknown, context: 'data' | 'login' = 'data'): DescribedError {
  const empty = { correlationId: null, retryAfterSeconds: null, fieldErrors: {} };

  // fetch itself failed (API down, no internet): there is no response and no reference
  if (error instanceof TypeError) {
    return {
      ...empty,
      kind: 'network',
      title: "Can't reach RondiTrack",
      message: 'Check your connection.',
    };
  }

  if (!(error instanceof ApiError)) {
    return {
      ...empty,
      kind: 'generic',
      title: 'Something went wrong',
      message: 'Something went wrong on our side. Please try again.',
    };
  }

  const correlationId = asString(error.problem?.correlationId);
  const base = { ...empty, correlationId };

  if (error.status === 429) {
    const seconds = parseRetryAfter(error.retryAfter);
    return {
      ...base,
      kind: 'rateLimited',
      title: 'Too many requests',
      message: rateLimitMessage(seconds),
      retryAfterSeconds: seconds,
    };
  }
  if (error.status === 401) {
    return context === 'login'
      ? { ...base, kind: 'badCredentials', title: 'Sign in failed', message: 'Email or password is incorrect.' }
      : { ...base, kind: 'sessionEnded', title: 'Session ended', message: 'Please sign in again.' };
  }
  if (error.status === 404) {
    return {
      ...base,
      kind: 'notFound',
      title: 'Stokvel not found',
      message: "This stokvel doesn't exist, or you are not a member of it.",
    };
  }
  if (error.status === 400) {
    const fieldErrors: Record<string, string[]> = {};
    const raw = error.problem?.errors;
    if (raw && typeof raw === 'object') {
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(raw)) {
        if (Array.isArray(value)) fieldErrors[key.toLowerCase()] = value.map(String);
      }
    }
    return { ...base, kind: 'validation', title: 'Please check your details', message: 'Some fields need your attention.', fieldErrors };
  }
  return {
    ...base,
    kind: 'generic',
    title: 'Something went wrong',
    message: 'Something went wrong on our side. Please try again in a moment.',
  };
}

// NEW: tests for the grouping function.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { UNKNOWN_CYCLE_KEY, groupContributionsByCycle } from './groupContributionsByCycle'

const cycles = [
  { id: 'c1', number: 1 },
  { id: 'c3', number: 3 },
  { id: 'c2', number: 2 },
]

const contributions = [
  { id: 'a', cycleId: 'c3' },
  { id: 'b', cycleId: 'c1' },
  { id: 'c', cycleId: 'c3' },
]

describe('groupContributionsByCycle', () => {
  it('puts the newest cycle first', () => {
    const groups = groupContributionsByCycle(cycles, contributions)
    expect(groups.map((g) => g.key)).toEqual(['c3', 'c2', 'c1'])
  })

  it('still shows a cycle that has no contributions', () => {
    const groups = groupContributionsByCycle(cycles, contributions)
    const empty = groups.find((g) => g.key === 'c2')
    expect(empty?.contributions).toEqual([])
  })

  it('keeps contributions in the order given, under the right cycle', () => {
    const groups = groupContributionsByCycle(cycles, contributions)
    expect(groups[0].contributions.map((c) => c.id)).toEqual(['a', 'c'])
    expect(groups[2].contributions.map((c) => c.id)).toEqual(['b'])
  })

  it('puts an unknown cycle id in a final Unknown cycle group and never drops it', () => {
    const withOrphan = [...contributions, { id: 'z', cycleId: 'missing' }]
    const groups = groupContributionsByCycle(cycles, withOrphan)
    const last = groups[groups.length - 1]
    expect(last.key).toBe(UNKNOWN_CYCLE_KEY)
    expect(last.cycle).toBeNull()
    expect(last.contributions.map((c) => c.id)).toEqual(['z'])
  })

  it('has no Unknown cycle group when nothing is orphaned', () => {
    const groups = groupContributionsByCycle(cycles, contributions)
    expect(groups.some((g) => g.key === UNKNOWN_CYCLE_KEY)).toBe(false)
  })

  it('the total number of contributions out equals the number in', () => {
    const withOrphan = [...contributions, { id: 'z', cycleId: 'missing' }]
    const groups = groupContributionsByCycle(cycles, withOrphan)
    const total = groups.reduce((sum, g) => sum + g.contributions.length, 0)
    expect(total).toBe(withOrphan.length)
  })
})

----- FILE: web\src\lib\groupContributionsByCycle.ts -----
// NEW: groups contributions under their cycle. A pure function: no state, no effects, called during render.
// Generic on purpose: it only needs a cycle id + number and a contribution cycleId, so the real types come from the API.
export const UNKNOWN_CYCLE_KEY = 'unknown-cycle'

export type CycleGroup<C, T> = {
  key: string // the cycle id (or "unknown-cycle"): open/closed state is keyed by this, never by position
  cycle: C | null // null only for the "Unknown cycle" group
  contributions: T[]
}

export function groupContributionsByCycle<
  C extends { id: string; number: number },
  T extends { cycleId: string },
>(cycles: readonly C[], contributions: readonly T[]): CycleGroup<C, T>[] {
  const knownIds = new Set(cycles.map((cycle) => cycle.id))
  const byCycle = new Map<string, T[]>()
  const orphans: T[] = []

  // Keep each contribution in the order the API gave it (newest first)
  for (const contribution of contributions) {
    if (knownIds.has(contribution.cycleId)) {
      const list = byCycle.get(contribution.cycleId) ?? []
      list.push(contribution)
      byCycle.set(contribution.cycleId, list)
    } else {
      orphans.push(contribution) // never dropped: it goes to "Unknown cycle"
    }
  }

  // Newest cycle first (highest number). A cycle with no contributions still gets a group.
  const groups: CycleGroup<C, T>[] = [...cycles]
    .sort((a, b) => b.number - a.number)
    .map((cycle) => ({ key: cycle.id, cycle, contributions: byCycle.get(cycle.id) ?? [] }))

  if (orphans.length > 0) {
    groups.push({ key: UNKNOWN_CYCLE_KEY, cycle: null, contributions: orphans })
  }
  return groups
}

----- FILE: web\src\lib\money.ts -----
// NEW: turns an integer number of cents into "R 150,50" without ever using fractional floats.
const zarFormatter = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-ZA', {
  style: 'currency',
  currency: 'ZAR',
})

export function formatCents(cents: number): string {
  // Reject 10.5, NaN, Infinity, or numbers too big to be exact
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(cents)) {
    throw new Error('not a whole number of cents')
  }

  // BigInt keeps everything as whole numbers, so there is no float rounding at all
  const big = BigInt(cents)
  const negative = big < 0n
  const abs = negative ? -big : big

  // Integer division and remainder: 15050 cents -> 150 rands and 50 cents
  const rands = abs / 100n
  const rest = abs % 100n

  // Build an exact decimal string like "150.50" (pad so 5 cents becomes "05")
  const decimal = `${negative ? '-' : ''}${rands}.${rest.toString().padStart(2, '0')}`

  // Intl accepts an exact decimal string, so it formats without turning it into a float
  return zarFormatter.format(decimal as `${number}`)
}

// Step 7 name: later files import formatRand, so it forwards to formatCents
export function formatRand(value: number): string {
  return formatCents(value)
}

import { QueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { ApiError } from '../api/apiError';

// Makes a fresh client (tests use this so each test starts clean)
export function createQueryClient() {
  return new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: {
      queries: {
        staleTime: 30_000,
        refetchOnWindowFocus: false,
        // 404, 403, 429 will not fix themselves, so never retry any 4xx
        retry: (failureCount, error) => {
          if (error instanceof ApiError && error.status >= 400 && error.status < 500) return false;
          return failureCount < 3;
        },
      },
    },
  });
}

// The one client the real app uses
export const queryClient = createQueryClient();

    expect(parseRandsToCents('-5')).toBeNull();

----- FILE: web\src\lib\rands.ts -----
// NEW 7.4: money <-> text for the form. Integer maths on text only: no parseFloat, no multiplying decimals,
// no toFixed, no rounding.

// DECISION: "1 500,50" IS accepted (spaces or no-break spaces for thousands, a comma for decimals).
// "1,500.50" is refused (ambiguous), and anything with more than 2 decimals is refused (it would need rounding).
export function parseRandsToCents(input: string): number | null {
  // remove spaces / no-break spaces, then turn a decimal comma into a dot
  const cleaned = input.trim().replace(/[\s\u00a0]/g, '').replace(',', '.');

  // digits, then optionally a dot with 1 or 2 digits
  const match = /^(\d+)(?:\.(\d{1,2}))?$/.exec(cleaned);
  if (!match) return null;

  const whole = match[1];
  const fraction = (match[2] ?? '').padEnd(2, '0'); // "5" -> "50", missing -> "00"

  // glue the digits as TEXT ("150" + "50" = "15050"), so no float maths ever happens
  const cents = parseInt(whole + fraction, 10);
  return Number.isSafeInteger(cents) ? cents : null;
}

// The reverse, for prefilling the input: 15050 -> "150.50", 15000 -> "150", 5 -> "0.05"
export function centsToInput(cents: number): string {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(cents) || cents < 0) {
    throw new RangeError('cents must be a non-negative whole number');
  }
  const digits = String(cents).padStart(3, '0'); // always at least 3 digits so we can split off 2 decimals
  const whole = digits.slice(0, -2);
  const fraction = digits.slice(-2);
  return fraction === '00' ? whole : `${whole}.${fraction}`;
}

// NEW: the ONLY place the role strings are compared, so a typo can't silently hide the section.
const TREASURER = 'Treasurer'
const MEMBER = 'Member'
const ADMIN = 'Admin'

export function isTreasurer(role: string): boolean {
  return role === TREASURER
}

// The role is always shown as words (never colour alone)
export function roleLabel(role: string): string {
  if (role === TREASURER) return "You're the Treasurer"
  if (role === MEMBER) return "You're a Member"
  if (role === ADMIN) return "You're an Admin"
  return `Unknown role: ${role}`
}

----- FILE: web\src\state\selectedStokvel.ts -----
import { useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';

// The selected stokvel id lives ONLY here (not in browser storage), so sign-out can clear it
let selectedId: string | null = null;
const subscribers = new Set<() => void>();

export function setSelectedStokvelId(id: string | null) {
  selectedId = id;
  subscribers.forEach((s) => s());
}

export function clearSelectedStokvel() {
  setSelectedStokvelId(null);
}

export function useSelectedStokvelId(): string | null {
  return useSyncExternalStore(
    (callback) => {
      subscribers.add(callback);
      return () => {
        subscribers.delete(callback);
      };
    },
    () => selectedId,
  );
}

// NEW: the theme "contract": which values exist and how components read/change them.
import { createContext, useContext } from 'react'

export type Theme = 'light' | 'dark' | 'system'
export const THEME_STORAGE_KEY = 'ronditrack-theme'

export type ThemeContextValue = { theme: Theme; setTheme: (theme: Theme) => void }
export const ThemeContext = createContext<ThemeContextValue | null>(null)

export function useTheme(): ThemeContextValue {
  const value = useContext(ThemeContext)
  if (!value) throw new Error('useTheme must be used inside ThemeProvider')
  return value
}

----- FILE: web\src\theme\ThemeProvider.tsx -----
// NEW: remembers the theme choice and puts the "dark" class on <html>. System follows the OS live.
import { useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { THEME_STORAGE_KEY, ThemeContext, type Theme } from './theme-context'

// Storage can be blocked (private browsing), so every read and write is guarded
function readStoredTheme(): Theme {
  try {
    const value = localStorage.getItem(THEME_STORAGE_KEY)
    if (value === 'light' || value === 'dark' || value === 'system') return value
  } catch {
    // storage blocked: fall back to the default
  }
  return 'system'
}

function applyTheme(theme: Theme) {
  const prefersDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches
  const dark = theme === 'dark' || (theme === 'system' && prefersDark)
  document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', dark)
  document.documentElement.style.colorScheme = dark ? 'dark' : 'light'
}

export function ThemeProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [theme, setThemeState] = useState<Theme>(readStoredTheme)

  useEffect(() => {
    applyTheme(theme)
    if (theme !== 'system') return
    // System mode: re-apply whenever the operating system switches light/dark
    const media = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')
    const onChange = () => applyTheme('system')
    media.addEventListener('change', onChange)
    return () => media.removeEventListener('change', onChange)
  }, [theme])

  function setTheme(next: Theme) {
    setThemeState(next)
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(THEME_STORAGE_KEY, next)
    } catch {
      // storage blocked: the choice still works until the page reloads
    }
  }

  return <ThemeContext.Provider value={{ theme, setTheme }}>{children}</ThemeContext.Provider>
}

----- FILE: web-next\README.md -----
# RondiTrack: web-next (Next.js 16)

The RondiTrack frontend rebuilt on Next.js 16.4.1 (App Router). Pages are Server Components. The browser never calls the API: the Next.js server does, with a token kept in an encrypted, HttpOnly cookie that the browser cannot read.

## Running it

1. Start the API: `dotnet run --project API --launch-profile http` (port 5134).
2. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in:
   - `API_BASE_URL` (e.g. `http://localhost:5134`)
   - `SESSION_SECRET`, made with `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`
3. In `web-next/`:
   ```bash
   npm install
   npm run gen:api   # regenerates src/types/schema.d.ts from the running API
   npm run dev       # http://localhost:3000
   npm test
   npm run build
   ```

Demo users (created by registering, then roles set in the database): `lerato.demo@example.com` (Treasurer of Ubuntu Savers, Member of Festive Grocery Club) and `sipho.demo@example.com` (Member of Ubuntu Savers only). Password for both: `Demo-password-123` (a throwaway demo value).

**Why neither variable starts with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`:** Next.js copies every `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable into the JavaScript sent to the browser. The API address and the encryption secret must stay on the server. A leaked `SESSION_SECRET` would let anyone forge a session cookie.

## API check

| # | Question | My answer |
|---|----------|-----------|
| 1 | Does the list return my role per stokvel? What for a user in no stokvels? | **No, so I fixed the API.** `GET /api/stokvels` is platform-admin only (403 for everyone else) and has no role. I added `GET /api/me/stokvels`: every stokvel I belong to with `myRole`, paid and owed this cycle and the next payout date. Lerato gets `Treasurer` for Ubuntu Savers and `Member` for Festive Grocery Club. A user in no stokvels gets **200 with `[]`** (tested). |
| 2 | Non-member vs missing id vs `not-a-guid`: same status? | **Yes, all three are 404.** A non-member and a missing id return the same problem+json (an existing test compares them). `not-a-guid` does not match the `{stokvelId:guid}` route, so it is a plain 404 with an empty body. The page shows the same not-found page for all three. |
| 3 | Which header carries the refresh token? | `Set-Cookie: rondi_refresh=<token>; expires=...; path=/api/auth; secure; samesite=strict; httponly`, read with `getSetCookie()` in `scripts/check-login.mjs`. Output: status 200, body keys `accessToken`, `expiresAtUtc`, `tokenType`. The refresh token is not in the body. |
| 4 | How long does the access token live? What when expired? | **10 minutes** (`Jwt:AccessTokenMinutes`). The API then returns 401 problem+json and the app sends the person to `/login?expired=1` (no refresh until Day 3). The session cookie lasts 7 days, but the access token inside it only works for 10 minutes. |
| 5 | Which IP does the API see for ten different people? | The Next.js server's IP, every time. The API has no login rate limit yet (6.1 gap), so nothing breaks today. See Known gaps. |
| 6 | Does `GET /stokvels/{id}` return member count and a cycle summary? | Member count: yes already. My role and the cycle summary: **no, so I added them** (`myRole` and `currentCycle` with collected amount and next payout date). |

**API fixes, with tests:** `GET /api/me`, `GET /api/me/stokvels` (new `MeController` and `MyStokvelsService`) and the extra fields on `GET /api/stokvels/{id}`. Tests are in `RondiTrack.Tests/MyStokvelsTests.cs`: me, 401 without a token, an empty list for a user in no stokvels, the role per stokvel (and nobody else's stokvels), paid/owed, and detail with role and cycle.

```
Test summary: total: 66, failed: 0, succeeded: 66, skipped: 0
```

**Assumption:** the data model has no payout schedule, so "next payout date" is the open cycle's start plus one period (weekly 7 days, fortnightly 14 days, monthly 1 month).

## Routes

| Route | What it shows | When there is nothing / not theirs |
|-------|---------------|------------------------------------|
| `/` | Redirects to `/dashboard/member` when signed in, `/login` when not | n/a |
| `/login` | Sign-in (Server Action + `useActionState`) | Wrong password shows the message and the reference |
| `/dashboard/member` | Every stokvel I belong to: paid, owed, next payout | Empty state |
| `/dashboard/treasurer` | Only stokvels where I am Treasurer, each linking to its detail page | Empty state (not an error, not a 403) |
| `/stokvels` | My stokvels as cards with my role | Empty state |
| `/stokvels/[id]` | Name, contribution, my role, member count, current cycle summary | `not-found.tsx` (same page for non-member, missing and malformed id) |

Data: `GET /api/me/stokvels` (one call builds the stokvel list and both dashboards, because it returns my role per stokvel), `GET /api/stokvels/{id}`, and `GET /api/me` at sign-in.

Because `loading.tsx` lets the page start streaming first, `notFound()` arrives as HTTP 200 with a `noindex` meta tag. That is how streaming works in Next.js 16, so I checked what the person sees, not the status code.

The sidebar has four links: Home, My stokvels, Member dashboard and Treasurer dashboard. `/stokvels/[id]` needs an id, so it is reached from the lists.

## The treasurer dashboard

RondiTrack has no "treasurer" users. It has users who are Treasurer of *some* stokvels, so one person can be Treasurer of one stokvel and Member of another. `/dashboard/treasurer` is therefore a filtered view that everyone may open, not a page behind a role check. It uses the pure function `stokvelsWhereTreasurer(list)` (`src/lib/stokvelsWhereTreasurer.ts`), tested in Vitest for a mixed list, a Treasurer-nowhere list and an empty list.

**Why the session stores no role:** a role belongs to a person *and a stokvel*. One role in the cookie or the token would be wrong for at least one of their stokvels, and it would go stale when a chairperson changes it. (The API's access token has no stokvel role either, for the same reason.) So the role comes from the API's answer for each stokvel, every time.

The sidebar shows all four links to everyone. Hiding "Treasurer" from people who are Treasurer nowhere would only be a convenience. The page is safe either way, because the API decides what each person may see.

## The client boundary

Files with `'use client'`, and the one reason each needs it:

- `src/components/StokvelCard.tsx`: the Show details toggle uses `useState`.
- `src/app/(auth)/login/LoginForm.tsx`: it uses `useActionState`, a React hook.
- `src/app/(app)/error.tsx`: error pages must be Client Components, and Try again uses `onClick`.

No Client Component imports `session.ts` or `api.ts`, and both start with `import 'server-only'`, so doing it breaks the build. `LoginForm` imports the Server Action from `actions.ts`. A `'use server'` import becomes only a reference to the server function, so the session code does not enter the browser bundle.

## Server-only proof

**Build error with `getSession` imported into `StokvelCard.tsx` (a Client Component):**

```
> Build error occurred
Error: Turbopack build failed with 3 errors:

./src/lib/session.ts:1:1
Error: 'server-only' cannot be imported from a Client Component module
> 1 | import 'server-only'; // Build error if a Client Component ever imports this file.
    | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  2 | import { cookies } from 'next/headers';

It should only be used from a Server Component.

Import traces:
  #3 [Client Component Browser]:
    ./src/lib/session.ts [Client Component Browser]
    ./src/components/StokvelCard.tsx [Client Component Browser]
    ./src/components/StokvelCard.tsx [Server Component]
    ./src/app/(app)/stokvels/page.tsx [Server Component]
```

**Build passing after I removed the import:**

```
â–² Next.js 16.4.1 (Turbopack)
âœ“ Compiled successfully in 9.7s
  Finished TypeScript in 11.0s ...
âœ“ Generating static pages using 1 worker (8/8) in 3.7s

Route (app)
â”Œ Æ’ /
â”œ â—‹ /_not-found
â”œ Æ’ /dashboard/member
â”œ Æ’ /dashboard/treasurer
â”œ Æ’ /login
â”œ Æ’ /stokvels
â”” Æ’ /stokvels/[id]
```

Without the guard, `session.ts` (the code that decrypts the cookie and builds the Bearer header, and needs the server-only `SESSION_SECRET`) would have been bundled into the JavaScript sent to every browser. The guard turns that mistake into a build error instead of a code review comment.

## Known gaps

- **Login rate limit (Q5):** the API has no login rate limit yet. Once it has a per-IP one, every sign-in will come from the Next.js server's IP, so all users would share one limit and could lock each other out. Not fixed this week.
- **Error messages in production:** Next.js hides the message of errors thrown in Server Components in production builds and shows only a digest. The friendly message and reference show fully in `npm run dev`; in `npm start` the page may show only the generic text and the digest as the reference.
- **Next payout date** is calculated (cycle start + one period) because the data model has no payout schedule.
- **Seed data:** my development database has leftover test data (for example Ubuntu Savers has 8 members with a maximum of 6, and several open cycles). The API treats the open cycle with the highest cycle number as the current one.
- **Platform admins:** the API lets a platform admin open any stokvel, so `myRole` can be null there and the page says so.
- **Roles** are set directly in the database, because there is still no endpoint to change a member's role (6.1 gap).
- No refresh, registration or route protection yet (Day 3). An expired token sends the person to `/login?expired=1`.
- API responses are cast to my own types (`src/lib/types.ts`), because the generated OpenAPI says the role and frequency enums are integers while the API sends strings.
- The `@theme` warning in `npm run build` comes from the Tailwind CSS setup of the generated template. The build succeeds.

----- FILE: web-next\src\app\(app)\actions.ts -----
'use server';

import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
import { deleteSession, getSession } from '@/lib/session';

// Tells the API to log out (with the refresh token), deletes our cookie, goes to /login.
export async function signOut(): Promise<void> {
  const session = await getSession();
  if (session) {
    try {
      // The API reads the refresh token from the "rondi_refresh" cookie on this request.
      await fetch(`${process.env.API_BASE_URL}/api/auth/logout`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { Cookie: `rondi_refresh=${session.refreshToken}` },
        cache: 'no-store',
      });
    } catch {
      // Even if the API is down, we still delete the local session below.
    }
  }
  await deleteSession();
  redirect('/login');
}

----- FILE: web-next\src\app\(app)\error.tsx -----
'use client'; // Error pages must be Client Components, and Try again needs an onClick.

type Props = {
  error: Error & { digest?: string };
  retry?: () => void; // the retry function; some Next 16 versions name it differently, so all names are accepted
  unstable_retry?: () => void;
  reset?: () => void;
};

// Shows the friendly message and its reference. Never a stack trace.
export default function AppError({ error, retry, unstable_retry, reset }: Props) {
  const tryAgain = retry ?? unstable_retry ?? reset;

  return (
    <div className="rounded border border-red-300 p-6">
      <h1 className="text-xl font-bold">Something went wrong</h1>
      <p className="mt-2 text-sm">{error.message}</p>
      {error.digest && <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-gray-500">Reference: {error.digest}</p>}
      <button type="button" onClick={() => tryAgain?.()} className="mt-4 rounded border px-3 py-1">
        Try again
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}

----- FILE: web-next\src\app\(auth)\login\actions.ts -----
'use server';

import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
import { createSession } from '@/lib/session';
import { correlationIdFrom } from '@/lib/errors';
import { loginMessageFor, messageFor } from '@/lib/errorMessages';

export type SignInState = { error?: string; correlationId?: string };

// The name of the refresh cookie the API sets (AuthConstants.RefreshCookieName).
const REFRESH_COOKIE_NAME = 'rondi_refresh';

// Finds the refresh token value inside the Set-Cookie headers of the login response.
function findRefreshToken(setCookies: string[]): string | null {
  const header = setCookies.find((c) => c.startsWith(`${REFRESH_COOKIE_NAME}=`));
  if (!header) return null;
  return header.split(';')[0].slice(REFRESH_COOKIE_NAME.length + 1);
}

export async function signIn(_prev: SignInState, formData: FormData): Promise<SignInState> {
  const email = String(formData.get('email') ?? '');
  const password = String(formData.get('password') ?? '');
  const base = process.env.API_BASE_URL;

  // 1. Ask the API to log in.
  const res = await fetch(`${base}/api/auth/login`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
    cache: 'no-store',
  });

  // Wrong password etc: show the friendly message and the reference.
  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = await res.json().catch(() => null);
    return { error: loginMessageFor(res.status), correlationId: correlationIdFrom(body) };
  }

  const body = (await res.json()) as { accessToken?: unknown };
  const accessToken = body.accessToken;
  const refreshToken = findRefreshToken(res.headers.getSetCookie());
  if (typeof accessToken !== 'string' || !refreshToken) {
    return { error: messageFor(500) };
  }

  // 2. Ask the API who this is.
  const meRes = await fetch(`${base}/api/me`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` },
    cache: 'no-store',
  });
  if (!meRes.ok) {
    const meBody = await meRes.json().catch(() => null);
    return { error: messageFor(meRes.status), correlationId: correlationIdFrom(meBody) };
  }
  const me = (await meRes.json()) as { id: string; email: string; fullName: string };

  // 3. Keep everything in the encrypted cookie. No role is stored.
  await createSession({
    accessToken,
    refreshToken,
    user: { id: me.id, email: me.email, displayName: me.fullName },
  });

  // redirect() works by throwing, so it must stay outside any try/catch.
  redirect('/dashboard/member');
}

----- FILE: web-next\src\lib\api.ts -----
import 'server-only'; // Only the server may build API calls with the token.
import createClient from 'openapi-fetch';
import { notFound, redirect } from 'next/navigation';
import type { paths } from '@/types/schema';
import { getSession } from './session';
import { ApiError, correlationIdFrom } from './errors';

// A typed API client that adds "Authorization: Bearer ..." from the session. No session = go to /login.
export async function api() {
  const session = await getSession();
  if (!session) redirect('/login');

  return createClient<paths>({
    baseUrl: process.env.API_BASE_URL,
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${session.accessToken}` },
  });
}

// Turns a result into data, or into the right response:
// 401 -> /login?expired=1, 404 -> not-found page, anything else -> ApiError (friendly message + reference).
// T is the shape I expect (from src/lib/types.ts).
export function unwrap<T>(result: { data?: unknown; error?: unknown; response: Response }): T {
  const { data, error, response } = result;
  if (response.status === 401) redirect('/login?expired=1');
  if (response.status === 404) notFound();
  if (!response.ok || data === undefined) {
    throw new ApiError(response.status, correlationIdFrom(error));
  }
  return data as T;
}

----- FILE: web-next\src\lib\errorMessages.ts -----
// Friendly messages for the person. If your 7.3 file has different wording, paste that wording here.
export function messageFor(status: number): string {
  switch (status) {
    case 400:
      return 'Something in that request was not right. Please check it and try again.';
    case 401:
      return 'Your session has ended. Please sign in again.';
    case 403:
      return 'You are not allowed to do that.';
    case 404:
      return "We couldn't find that.";
    case 429:
      return 'Too many attempts. Please wait a bit and try again.';
    default:
      return 'Something went wrong on our side. Please try again.';
  }
}

// Message for a failed sign-in (a 401 here means wrong email or password, not an ended session).
export function loginMessageFor(status: number): string {
  return status === 401 ? 'Your email or password is wrong.' : messageFor(status);
}

// Adds the reference number so support can find the request in the API log.
export function withReference(message: string, correlationId?: string): string {
  return correlationId ? `${message} (Reference: ${correlationId})` : message;
}

----- FILE: web-next\src\lib\errors.ts -----
import { messageFor, withReference } from './errorMessages';

// The one error type for "anything else" from the API. Its message is already friendly and has the reference.
export class ApiError extends Error {
  status: number;
  correlationId?: string;

  constructor(status: number, correlationId?: string) {
    super(withReference(messageFor(status), correlationId));
    this.name = 'ApiError';
    this.status = status;
    this.correlationId = correlationId;
  }
}

// Finds the correlationId in a problem+json body (the API puts it there).
export function correlationIdFrom(body: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (body && typeof body === 'object' && 'correlationId' in body) {
    const id = (body as Record<string, unknown>).correlationId;
    if (typeof id === 'string') return id;
  }
  return undefined;
}

----- FILE: web-next\src\lib\format.ts -----
// Turns rands into text, e.g. 150 -> "R 150,00". (The API sends rands, so this replaces formatCents.)
export function formatMoney(amount: number): string {
  return new Intl.NumberFormat('en-ZA', { style: 'currency', currency: 'ZAR' }).format(amount);
}

// Turns an ISO date into a short readable date.
export function formatDate(iso: string | null | undefined): string {
  if (!iso) return 'Not set';
  return new Date(iso).toLocaleDateString('en-ZA', { year: 'numeric', month: 'short', day: 'numeric' });
}

----- FILE: web-next\src\lib\session.ts -----
import 'server-only'; // Build error if a Client Component ever imports this file.
import { cookies } from 'next/headers';
import { EncryptJWT, jwtDecrypt } from 'jose';

// Everything we keep about the signed-in person. NO role here: a role belongs to a person AND a stokvel,
// so it comes from the API for each stokvel.
export type SessionData = {
  accessToken: string;
  refreshToken: string;
  user: { id: string; email: string; displayName: string };
};

const COOKIE_NAME = 'session';
const MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 60 * 60 * 24 * 7; // 7 days (same as the API's refresh token)

// Reads the 32-byte secret from .env.local. Stops loudly if it is missing or the wrong size.
function getKey(): Uint8Array {
  const secret = process.env.SESSION_SECRET;
  if (!secret) throw new Error('SESSION_SECRET is not set');
  const key = Buffer.from(secret, 'base64');
  if (key.length !== 32) throw new Error('SESSION_SECRET must be 32 bytes, base64 encoded');
  return new Uint8Array(key);
}

// Checks that decrypted data really has the shape of SessionData.
function isSessionData(value: unknown): value is SessionData {
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return false;
  const v = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  const u = v.user as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
  return (
    typeof v.accessToken === 'string' &&
    typeof v.refreshToken === 'string' &&
    !!u &&
    typeof u.id === 'string' &&
    typeof u.email === 'string' &&
    typeof u.displayName === 'string'
  );
}

// Encrypts the data (dir + A256GCM) and stores it in the HttpOnly cookie.
export async function createSession(data: SessionData): Promise<void> {
  const jwt = await new EncryptJWT({ data })
    .setProtectedHeader({ alg: 'dir', enc: 'A256GCM' })
    .setIssuedAt()
    .setExpirationTime(`${MAX_AGE_SECONDS}s`)
    .encrypt(getKey());

  const store = await cookies();
  store.set('session', jwt, {
    httpOnly: true, // JavaScript in the browser cannot read it
    secure: true, // only sent over HTTPS (Chrome also allows it on localhost)
    sameSite: 'lax',
    path: '/',
    maxAge: MAX_AGE_SECONDS,
  });
}

// Reads the cookie. A bad cookie (cannot decrypt, wrong shape) counts as no session at all.
export async function getSession(): Promise<SessionData | null> {
  const store = await cookies();
  const token = store.get(COOKIE_NAME)?.value;
  if (!token) return null;
  try {
    const { payload } = await jwtDecrypt(token, getKey());
    return isSessionData(payload.data) ? payload.data : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

// Deletes the cookie (used when signing out).
export async function deleteSession(): Promise<void> {
  const store = await cookies();
  store.delete(COOKIE_NAME);
}

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { stokvelsWhereTreasurer } from './stokvelsWhereTreasurer';
import type { MyStokvel, Role } from './types';

// Small helper to build a test stokvel.
const make = (id: string, myRole: Role): MyStokvel => ({
  id,
  name: `Stokvel ${id}`,
  contributionAmount: 100,
  frequency: 'Monthly',
  memberCount: 3,
  myRole,
  paidThisCycle: 0,
  owedThisCycle: 100,
  nextPayoutDateUtc: null,
  currentCycle: null,
});

describe('stokvelsWhereTreasurer', () => {
  it('keeps only the Treasurer stokvels in a mixed list', () => {
    const result = stokvelsWhereTreasurer([make('1', 'Treasurer'), make('2', 'Member'), make('3', 'Treasurer')]);
    expect(result.map((s) => s.id)).toEqual(['1', '3']);
  });

  it('returns an empty list when the person is Treasurer nowhere', () => {
    expect(stokvelsWhereTreasurer([make('1', 'Member'), make('2', 'Member')])).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('returns an empty list for an empty list', () => {
    expect(stokvelsWhereTreasurer([])).toEqual([]);
  });
});

----- FILE: web-next\src\lib\stokvelsWhereTreasurer.ts -----
import type { MyStokvel } from './types';

// Pure filter: keeps only the stokvels where the person is Treasurer.
// The role comes from the API's answer for each stokvel, never from the token or the session.
export function stokvelsWhereTreasurer(list: MyStokvel[]): MyStokvel[] {
  return list.filter((s) => s.myRole === 'Treasurer');
}
